title: Train/Test Splits & Cross-Validation — Rows Are Not Always Independent
key_insight: Group-aware splits keep related rows together. Time-aware splits always train on the past and validate on the future.
body:
## Rows Are Not Always Independent

The same patient appears in both training and validation, or tomorrow’s records teach a model judged on yesterday. The split leaks identity or time.

Group-aware splits keep related rows together. Time-aware splits always train on the past and validate on the future.

Match the split to real deployment. A random split answers the wrong question when requests arrive in groups or chronological waves.
common_mistakes: Using the test set to choose model settings.
Randomly splitting time-ordered or grouped records.
Reporting only the best fold instead of the full variation.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Rows Are Not Always Independent” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Without a fair split, every model comparison can be confidently wrong.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Rows Are Not Always Independent” story, explain Train/Test Splits & Cross-Validation without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
